FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2 YEARS

Vehicles & Sounds flashcards.

Twenty vehicle cards for toddlers who stop, point and shout "car!" at every window. Make the sounds together, then play spot-the-vehicle for real — wheels, wings and one very loud siren.

These cards belong to Toddler 6 on the Kiddo School learning path.

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Say it, then make the noise

    Name the vehicle first — bus — then the sound: beep beep. Your toddler will race to copy the sound before the word, and both count as winning.

  2. 02

    Sort them: road, sky, water

    Lay out a few cards and group them — which ones drive, which ones fly, which ones float? Your toddler does the pointing; you do the naming.

  3. 03

    Play spot-the-vehicle

    Keep two or three cards by the window. When a real bus rumbles past, grab the bus card and match it. Real traffic becomes part of the game.

  4. 04

    Follow your toddler's favourite

    Most toddlers pick one vehicle and want it again and again. That is how they learn — let them wear the digger card out.

      Car Flashcard for Toddlers

      The first vehicle most toddlers name, usually shouted from a car seat with total delight. This card gives the word a picture to stick to — red body, four wheels, beep beep.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Gives the everyday hero of the driveway its proper name and noise.

      Make the noise

      Vroom a toy car over your knees, braking sharply at each knee-bend.

      What it teaches

      The easiest engine sound there is, and often the first one said.

      How to print it

      Print two; cars get loved hard and lost under sofas.

      Tip for today

      Sound the engine from cold; a slow, sputtery start earns the vroom.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Car lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Bus Flashcard for Toddlers

      Big, boxy and impossible to miss, the bus is usually a vehicle your toddler has actually ridden. The wheels-on-the-bus song is practically built into this card.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Names the giant that carries the whole neighbourhood past your stop.

      Make the noise

      Line up the shoes as passengers and beep-beep them off one by one.

      What it teaches

      Repeating bus songs sneaks counting and naming into ordinary play.

      How to print it

      Full size, no shrinking — buses refuse to be small.

      Tip for today

      Beep twice for greeting, once for leaving; buses have manners.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bus lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Truck Flashcard for Toddlers

      A big truck with a trailer to point out, and a low rumble to imitate. Trucks earn respect from toddlers because they are bigger than everything else on the road.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Explains the biggest, loudest thing that ever passes your toddler's window.

      Make the noise

      Rumble across the rug on all fours, fully loaded and honking gently.

      What it teaches

      Big vehicles earn big words — rumble stretches a toddler vocabulary nicely.

      How to print it

      Card stock only; trucks get pushed across everything.

      Tip for today

      Deliveries need a destination; let them choose where the load lands.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Truck lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Fire Truck Flashcard for Toddlers

      Red, ladder on top, siren on the roof — the fire truck is the loudest hero in the set. Nee-naw is one of the easiest and most satisfying sounds your toddler will ever make.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Turns a passing siren from scary noise into a nameable, knowable friend.

      Make the noise

      Wee-oo down the hallway with a rolled magazine megaphone, rescuing nothing in particular.

      What it teaches

      Sirens become information once your toddler can name them calmly.

      How to print it

      Laminate this one; emergency play involves surprising amounts of water.

      Tip for today

      Real sirens get one calm name-out-loud, then back to breakfast.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Fire Truck lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Ambulance Flashcard for Toddlers

      A white van with lights and a very important job. The sound is the same fun nee-naw as the fire truck, which makes the two cards a natural pair for matching games.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Names the van that arrives when something hurts, and makes it friendly.

      Make the noise

      Load one unwell doll into a shoebox stretcher and drive it slowly, wee-oo.

      What it teaches

      Helping play grows gentle hands while the siren grows loud lungs.

      How to print it

      White vans show every smudge — use your cleanest paper.

      Tip for today

      Keep the wee-oo gentle at bedtime; even sirens whisper at night.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ambulance lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Police Car Flashcard for Toddlers

      A police car with bold stripes and lights on top, ready to go fast. Toddlers love the pattern on the side almost as much as the siren.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Explains who zooms to help, with the loudest thank-you siren going.

      Make the noise

      Direct traffic across the kitchen tiles, one raised hand, one slow woo-woo.

      What it teaches

      Three noisy vehicles sound alike — telling sirens apart is real listening work.

      How to print it

      Print it beside its siren cousins so the trio stays together.

      Tip for today

      One siren at a time keeps the game fun instead of loud.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Police Car lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Motorcycle Flashcard for Toddlers

      Fast, lean and loud, the motorcycle is the vehicle that gets a "vroom" from two doors down. The two wheels and the rider give you extra things to spot and name.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Names the fast, lean machine that zips past fences and hedges.

      Make the noise

      Brum-brum around the table legs, helmet on (a colander, naturally).

      What it teaches

      Fast sounds said fast build mouth-muscle speed for later words.

      How to print it

      Sturdy paper for this one; it travels in the buggy pocket.

      Tip for today

      Helmets first, even colander ones; the habit starts in pretend.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Motorcycle lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Bicycle Flashcard for Toddlers

      A friendly bicycle with pedals, basket and a little bell — ring ring. It is the vehicle your toddler already knows from the park, which makes this card feel like an old friend.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Gives your toddler's own ride a bigger, noisier cousin on paper.

      Make the noise

      Ring a spoon against a mug for a bell and pedal your thumbs.

      What it teaches

      Ring-push-go teaches cause and effect faster than any explanation.

      How to print it

      Slot it beside the scooter card for a two-wheeler corner.

      Tip for today

      Bell means "coming through" — practise the warning, then the zoom.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bicycle lesson on the Learning Path.

      Train Flashcard for Toddlers

      Chugga-chugga-choo-choo — the train brings its own song, and toddlers are the choir. Point out the carriages in a row: one train, lots of cars behind it.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Long and connected, the train crosses fields and tunnels in one line.

      Make the noise

      Choo-choo in a family conga line, doors as tunnels, dinner as the station.

      What it teaches

      Long sounds, long lines — trains sneak sequencing into the fun.

      How to print it

      Landscape orientation, obviously — trains refuse portrait.

      Tip for today

      Stations need announcements — invent one destination per lap.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Train lesson on the Learning Path.

      Tractor Flashcard for Toddlers

      Slow, big-wheeled and built for mud, the tractor is the star of any country walk and many a farm book. Its low put-put sound is easy to copy and hard to say without smiling.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Explains the slow, mighty machine behind every field and farm book.

      Make the noise

      Putt-putt across the room, hauling a small saucepan behind on a string.

      What it teaches

      Slow vehicles teach slow words — putt-putt is patience with an engine.

      How to print it

      Thick card again; tractor cards plough through sticky fingers.

      Tip for today

      Putt slower when excited; tractors never hurry, and that is the charm.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Tractor lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Excavator Flashcard for Toddlers

      The excavator — digger to every toddler alive — has an arm and a bucket that scoops. This is the card that gets requested at breakfast, lunch and dinner.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Celebrates the digging machine — star of every building site passed.

      Make the noise

      Excavate dry oats from mixing bowl to cake tin, one rumbling scoop at a time.

      What it teaches

      Dumping and refilling is physics practice, though nobody needs to know.

      How to print it

      Print a spare; the digger years run long.

      Tip for today

      Name the arm, the bucket and the cab; parts beat whole words.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Excavator lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Dump Truck Flashcard for Toddlers

      A dump truck carries a load and then tips it out — which is also exactly what your toddler does with any container they can lift. Built-in kinship.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Gives permission for the world's best game — load, drive, tip, repeat.

      Make the noise

      Reverse slowly, beeping at every corner, then tip your cargo grandly.

      What it teaches

      Tipping is a finale; this card teaches the joy of a job finished.

      How to print it

      Strong paper; dump trucks are the hardest-working card here.

      Tip for today

      The beep-backup warning is a real road sound — teach it early.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Dump Truck lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Airplane Flashcard for Toddlers

      A plane with wide wings, flying high — the one vehicle your toddler sees mostly as a tiny dot in the sky, which is exactly why the card is exciting: a close-up look.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Points at that white line in the sky and gives it a name.

      Make the noise

      Arms wide, one landing lap of the lounge, whooshing down to a gentle stop.

      What it teaches

      Up, across and down — movement words ride along with the whoosh.

      How to print it

      Save this one for long journeys; airport waiting loves it.

      Tip for today

      Turbulence is optional; wobbly landings get the biggest laughs.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Airplane lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Helicopter Flashcard for Toddlers

      A helicopter with spinning blades that go whup-whup-whup. Round windows and a funny tail make it easy to tell apart from the plane — a good pair for compare-and-point games.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Introduces the machine that hovers — no roads, just sky.

      Make the noise

      Whop-whop one spinning hand overhead, hovering, then landing on your own nose.

      What it teaches

      Hover means staying still while moving — a trick worth naming.

      How to print it

      Tape it beside the airplane card; the skies get busy together.

      Tip for today

      Freeze mid-hover on purpose; stillness games calm busy bodies.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Helicopter lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Boat Flashcard for Toddlers

      A little boat bobbing on the water with a friendly hull to point at. It is the vehicle for bath time, puddles and pond days, and "splash" comes free with it.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Puts a name to the nightly bathtub fleet, flagship included.

      Make the noise

      Row your arms across the rug, splash-song included, docking at the bookshelf.

      What it teaches

      Floating versus sinking is tomorrow's science, seeded at bath time.

      How to print it

      Two copies recommended — bath cards end up wet eventually.

      Tip for today

      Boats pass on the left — declare this confidently and sail on.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Boat lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Ship Flashcard for Toddlers

      A big ship with containers stacked high — the boat's enormous cousin. Big versus small is the obvious game when this card and the boat card sit side by side.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Brings the harbour's biggest visitor home in card form.

      Make the noise

      Stack a cargo of toy animals high and toot grandly around the rug.

      What it teaches

      Big loads tip over — early physics arrives by accident, hilariously.

      How to print it

      Go big on this one; ships fill a whole horizon.

      Tip for today

      A trip to see actual water upgrades this card enormously.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ship lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Rocket Flashcard for Toddlers

      Five, four, three, two, one — the rocket is the loudest countdown in the set and the fastest way to get a whole family shouting together. Up, up and away.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Sends the count to three into the stratosphere, toddler aboard.

      Make the noise

      Crouch, count backwards from three, and blast off across the room on tiptoes.

      What it teaches

      Counting backwards is a genuinely new skill, disguised as launch fuel.

      How to print it

      Reserve the biggest empty floor; rockets need runway.

      Tip for today

      The smallest crew member shouts blast off, non-negotiable.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Rocket lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Taxi Flashcard for Toddlers

      A yellow taxi with a sign on top — the car that honks in every city book. If your toddler has ridden one, this card is a memory; if not, it is a small yellow mystery to enjoy.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Adds a generous idea to cars — stopping for whoever waves.

      Make the noise

      Vroom each toy passenger from shelf to windowsill, one polite destination request per trip.

      What it teaches

      Pick-up, ride, drop-off — sequencing hides inside every taxi trip.

      How to print it

      Keep it near the car card for an instant traffic jam.

      Tip for today

      A "thank you, driver" at drop-off plants manners in traffic.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Taxi lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Van Flashcard for Toddlers

      The van arrives with boxes and parcels, which makes it the most exciting vehicle of the day whenever it actually stops at your door. Grey, practical and secretly fascinating.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Welcomes the parcel van, the most exciting arrival of any day.

      Make the noise

      Deliver one folded flannel per room, vrooming between stops, knocking at each door.

      What it teaches

      Vans arrive, knock and leave — daily comings and goings, named.

      How to print it

      Pin it near the front door, where deliveries happen.

      Tip for today

      Knock before every delivery — the knock is the game's best part.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Van lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · VEHICLES & SOUNDS · AGES 2 YEARS

      Scooter Flashcard for Toddlers

      A bright scooter with two small wheels and a handlebar — the vehicle your toddler will want to ride before they can say the word. One foot up, one foot push.

      Teaching tips

      What this card teaches

      Sets up the ride they will ask for, ideally today.

      Make the noise

      Zing to the door, brake hard, wobble dramatically, then zing onward.

      What it teaches

      Stopping completely is the hard half — this card celebrates it.

      How to print it

      Two copies — one for the hall, one for wherever scooting happens.

      Tip for today

      Full stops earn the zoom — praise the pause, not the speed.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Scooter lesson on the Learning Path.
